claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: The source marks exactly the original descent bottoms before performing any moves. Moving them to the front in increasing index order reverses their order, while removal and reinsertion preserve the relative order of every unmarked element. This proves the displayed map for arbitrary permutations. The exact checker also compared it with a literal sequential MoveToFront implementation on all 409113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9.
claims.witness: The source example (4,3,1,5,2,6,10,8,9,7) maps to (7,8,2,1,3,4,5,6,10,9), exactly as the formula predicts.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic derivation from the authorized source pseudocode, followed by exhaustive exact comparison through n=9.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: All entries of the active prefix are at most i, so i is unmarked. If R is nonempty, its first entry is marked because it follows i; a later r_j is unmarked precisely when r_{j-1}<r_j. Claim 0 therefore leaves exactly A(R) to the right of i. The already-fixed increasing suffix remains unmarked and fixed. Iteration gives the stated extinction time, including h(empty)=0. The stack computation was independently checked against literal A-iteration for all 409113 standardized words through length 9.
claims.witness: For (2,4,1,3,5), with i=4 and R=(1,3), the successive states are (1,2,4,3,5) and (3,1,2,4,5); meanwhile (1,3) maps under A to (3) and then empty, so both phase counts equal 2.
claims.search_method: General one-round analysis followed by induction on the number of rounds; exhaustive exact phase and stack checks through active-prefix size 9.

claims.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case number of nontrivial rounds, then W(n)<=n(n-1)/2. Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: Partition the execution into phases for maxima n,n-1,...,2, assigning length zero to an already-fixed maximum. Claim 1 applies in every phase. For nonempty R, A omits its first entry, so h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Every nontrivial round belongs to one such phase, hence W(n)<=sum_{i=2}^n(i-1)=n(n-1)/2. Dividing by n^2 gives a uniform bound below 1/2, which rules out little-omega(n^2) for every family.
claims.witness: The exhaustive values through n=9 all satisfy the bound; n=4 attains equality W(4)=6=4*3/2.
claims.search_method: Universal phase partition and finite-sum argument, with exhaustive exact sanity checks through n=9.

claims.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
claims.evidence: With B_0 empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m), the round formula inductively gives T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 through t=n-1. Thus n first becomes fixed after n-1 rounds. Put m=n-1. Since B_m=mC with C=T(B_{m-1}) nonempty, A(B_m)=A(C), so h(B_m)=h(C). The stated decreasing-stack invariant has maximum label q characterized by q(q+1)/2<=m<(q+1)(q+2)/2; therefore the next maximum requires q further rounds. This is exactly the claimed floor expression. The full trajectory, equality h(C)=q, and both cases of the stack-label invariant were checked exactly for every 3<=n<=501.
claims.witness: For n=3 the bound is 3 and the trajectory (3,1,2)->(1,3,2)->(2,1,3)->(1,2,3) attains it.
claims.search_method: Induction using the exact round map and the stated triangular decreasing-stack invariant, supplemented by exact integer checks for 499 consecutive values of n.
